note: Printed-only assertions. Wire list image-read at 300 dpi against PDF p.37 and matches the 28 printed wires; ER-37 is prose only and changes no wire. No initial dial setting is printed for this experiment, so the dial starts where the machine constructs it. Script follows the printed procedure: turn power on, let it transmit, turn power off ('until the power is turned off'). Untils assert that light 6 lights and relay 3 operates soon after power on (p.31 'immediately begin transmitting'), that light 6 goes dark again after a flash (ER-37 'flashes on very briefly'; p.31 'remain on'), that a second flash follows, and, after a further 10 s run, that light 6 still flashes and relay 3 still operates ('continue to transmit'); the two expects after power off assert light 6 dark and relay 3 released. Relay 3 'on' is read as relay3=no (armature pulled in). Sequential untils with 3000 ms caps do not tie a flash to a dot, a dash, or a dial position. Left for Step 7 as derived: the SOS on/off sequence against dial position (programs.json printedUnprinted); the nine-element count implied by the printed Morse table 'S: · · · / O: — — — / S: · · ·'; the 'remain on longer for a dash than for a dot' duration comparison; and the ER-37 slowed revolution ('slow the rotary switch down by holding the pointer knob back during one revolution'), whose per-dot assertions would need the derived dot-to-position mapping. At the profile's run rate the three S contacts give one unbroken light-6 'on' (the ~21 ms gaps between the S contacts never reach dim; the ~25 ms gaps between the O contacts dip to dim for about 4 ms). ER-37 says only 'almost indistinguishable', so the full merge is a simulator result left for Step 7; relay 3, self-interrupting through its own N.C. contact (3E/3H, 3J/6A), buzzes on each contact and falls quiet in each gap. Rotary geometry, run rate, coast, and fitted motor resistances remain profile fallbacks O-R1, O-R3, and O-R5. Trips the knife-edge trigger (minTickGap 4 below 6); the bless gate's robustness check held.
